notable_absence.finding: This page's own 'Description: What is RBAC' section defines the abstract two-tier model exactly as roles.md/authorization-overview.md do ('access privileges are assigned to fixed roles ... according to defined privileges'), but every concrete requirement stated for the rest of the page - the Minimal Eventing RBAC role list, the Beyond Minimal additions, the Bindings requirement, the SQL++ SELECT requirement, and the multi-tenancy walkthrough - is expressed purely in terms of ROLE names (Data Reader, Data Writer, Data DCP Reader, Data Monitor, Eventing Manage Scope Functions, Query Select), never a named privilege. This is a second, independent confirmation of the registry's already-recorded finding (docs-issues/server-rbac-privilege-tier-is-abstract-only, and hasPrivilege's own note) that Server's privilege tier is asserted in the abstract and never instantiated concretely anywhere in the corpus - eventing-rbac.md had every opportunity to be the page that finally names one, given how granular its role list is, and does not.

cross_component_finding: This page's own text contains a probable typo worth surfacing for downstream editorial review, though extraction leaves it uncorrected and unfiled: 'If you plan to use SQL++ consider adding at lease SELECT privileges' (likely intended: 'at least'). Separately, roles.md's canonical label for the role this page calls 'Eventing / Manage Scope Function' is actually 'Eventing Manage Scope Functions' (plural Functions, no slash) - a label variant confined to this one page rather than a Server-vs-Capella difference.
cross_product_finding: Server's minimal-RBAC role list requires **Data DCP Reader** specifically so a Function can 'start a Database Change Protocol (DCP) stream' on its Listen To Location - i.e. the classic RBAC model treats DCP-stream access as a separately grantable capability, distinct from ordinary Data Reader/Data Writer key-value access. The Capella twin (cloud/eventing/eventing-rbac.md, already extracted) gates the equivalent 'Source / Mutation' surface with 'Data Read and Eventing Manage' and never names a DCP-specific privilege at all. No page in either tree states that Capella's Eventing Manage privilege subsumes DCP-stream access, so the two models cannot be safely treated as isomorphic even though they gate what both pages call the same three functional surfaces (source/mutation keyspace, metadata/storage keyspace, bindings) - this looks structural (Capella's privilege catalogue is coarser by design, one privilege standing in for several Server roles at once) rather than a documentation gap in one tree or the other.
